With ls_workspace an adaptive run is labelled with the least-squares workspace although the kernel does not use it (stated in the function's doc). None of these options is on in any run of the node. Doc comments outside the write list that cite line numbers of the driver (tests/stage_clients_krylov_v17_contracts.rs:214, tests/residual_acceptance_contract.rs:41) are 141 to 227 lines off after the edit.
findings.correction: State that the sentence covers the GMRES-into solves of the policy and that the measured validity (V) covers the default workspace settings. The stale line references are cosmetic and outside the node's write list.

findings.claim: Reviewer's own side effects during the review (all reverted)
findings.evidence: (a) My first build of the commit-A export used the given CARGO_TARGET_DIR with the export inside it. Cargo's unit names do not depend on the source path, so the build replaced the head artifacts of core, krylov, integrators and mf_adaptive_measure, and cargo then reported the builder's worktree as up to date while the binary was the commit-A one. Repaired: export files touched, the node's targets rebuilt from the worktree; the measurement binary is again a030068160c9... (its hash before my build), no fingerprint or .d file of the target directory names review-scratch, later export builds used review-scratch/target-export. (b) A session hook created .mypy_cache in mf_adaptive/ and mf_stage_solve/ of the builder's worktree when Python files were opened (git-ignored); both were moved to review-scratch/moved_out_of_worktree. End state: git status --short --ignored empty, HEAD 28e7fca4, no file in the worktree newer than the builder's last commit; target directory 3.6 GB.
findings.correction: For the orchestrator: one CARGO_TARGET_DIR must not serve two source trees at different commits; cargo decides freshness by modification time and silently reuses the other tree's artifacts. The builder's single-worktree runs are not affected (binaries reproduced byte for byte).
